title: Station setup and grounding
blurb: Wire a station correctly: meters, power, computer audio links, RF bonding, keyers and hotspots.

T4A01.why: Mobile radios run on **13.8 V**, and a 50 W FM radio draws about **12 A** on transmit, so the supply must deliver that.
T4A01.trap: 24 V is wrong for a mobile radio, and 4 A is too little current.

T4A02.why: A meter only reads correctly within the **frequency and power range** it was built for.

T4A03.why: At 12 A, wire resistance drops real voltage (V = I × R). **Short, heavy wire** keeps the drop small when transmitting.

T4A04.why: FT8 uses the computer's **sound card**: radio audio out and in connect to the **computer running the FT8 software**.
T4A04.trap: No terminal node controller or website is involved.

T4A05.why: An RF power meter measures what goes to the antenna, so it sits **in the feed line between transmitter and antenna**.
T4A05.trap: On the DC supply it would only see DC, not RF output.

T4A06.why: The interface carries **receive audio, transmit audio, and transmitter keying** (push-to-talk).

T4A07.why: Receive audio leaves the radio's **speaker connector** and enters the computer's **line in**.
T4A07.trap: Push-to-talk is keying, not an audio connection.

T4A08.why: RF travels on a conductor's surface, so a wide **flat copper strap** gives the lowest-loss bond.

T4A09.why: Time = capacity ÷ load: **ampere-hours ÷ average current**. A 100 Ah battery at 10 A lasts 10 hours.
T4A09.trap: Don't use peak consumption or squared current.

T4A10.why: A hotspot connects your radio to a **digital voice or data network** over the internet.

T4A11.why: Run the negative lead to the **battery / chassis ground**, the vehicle's proper return point.
T4A11.trap: Random metal or a mounting bracket gives a poor, unpredictable return.

T4A12.why: An electronic keyer **assists in sending Morse code** by hand.
